title: Kernel change regression signal tagging (kernel selection + version tags in telemetry)
creator: Noah Patel
description:
Goal
Add stable, low-cardinality kernel selection/version tags to runtime telemetry so perf-canary regressions can be correlated to (a) kernel rollouts (new fused-attn, GEMM variants, kv-cache paths) and (b) auto-selection changes (heuristics picking different kernels based on seq len / batch / dtype / hardware).

Why
We can already detect p95 latency/tokens/sec regressions per model, but triage is slow when we can’t quickly answer: “Did the runtime switch kernels?” Kernel-level changes are one of the most common sources of tail regressions and throughput shifts, and can also be region/SKU-specific.

Non-goals
- Exposing fine-grained per-layer kernel traces (too expensive / high overhead)
- Adding high-cardinality identifiers (kernel binary hash per build, per-request compile cache keys)
- Anything that logs customer inputs (explicitly prohibited)

Proposed tags (telemetry dimensions)
These tags must be:
- Stable across requests for the same runtime build/config
- Small bounded value set (safe for metrics + traces)
- Sufficient to correlate regressions to major kernel selection behavior

1) runtime.kernel_set
- Definition: logical bundle name for the kernel package shipped with the runtime.
- Examples: "ks_2026_01_15", "ks_2026_02_03"
- Notes: this is the primary correlation key for “kernel rollout happened”. It’s intentionally not a git SHA.

2) runtime.attn_impl
- Definition: attention implementation family used for the request path.
- Allowed values (initial): "flash_v2", "flash_v3", "xformers", "sdpa", "baseline"
- Notes: keep this small; don’t include sub-variants.

3) runtime.gemm_impl
- Definition: GEMM implementation family for main matmuls.
- Allowed values (initial): "cutlass", "cublaslt", "triton", "torch"

4) runtime.kv_cache_impl
- Definition: KV cache management path.
- Allowed values: "paged", "contiguous", "none"

5) runtime.kernel_select_policy
- Definition: indicates whether selection was forced or auto.
- Allowed values: "auto", "forced_config", "forced_flag"
- Rationale: makes it obvious when a regression is tied to toggling a force flag or policy.

6) runtime.kernel_select_reason (trace-only; optional)
- Definition: very small enumerated reason code describing why a kernel family was selected.
- Allowed values (initial): "seq_len_bucket", "dtype", "sm_arch", "batch_bucket", "compat_fallback"
- Constraint: trace-only to avoid metrics cardinality; sampling enforced.

Where these tags show up
- Metrics: perf-canary histograms/counters for runtime-only latency, queueing time, tokens/sec should include at least runtime.kernel_set and runtime.attn_impl.
- Traces: attach all tags above at the request span (and optionally on the runtime execution span).
- Logs: do NOT include per-request kernel debug dumps by default; gated behind a short-lived flag for oncall only.

Cardinality / safety constraints
- Do not include: kernel binary hash, per-GPU UUID, compile cache keys, per-layer names, model internal layer ids.
- Keep tag value sets bounded and documented; any new values require a quick review in #eng-platform (telemetry).
- Sampling: runtime.kernel_select_reason only on 1% of canary traffic (or lower) and never on customer traffic unless explicitly enabled.

Implementation plan
1) Define the canonical tag names and allowed values in runtime telemetry schema (with ownership in Serving Runtime).
2) Plumb kernel selection output (from the kernel registry / selector) to the request context.
3) Emit tags:
   - Metrics via the per-model metrics aggregation helper (consistent naming + histogram buckets).
   - Tracing tags on root request spans.
4) Add a validation test in perf-canary CI smoke (ENG-4884) to ensure tags are present and non-empty for canary traffic.
5) Update dashboard panels to show overlays/breakdowns by runtime.kernel_set and runtime.attn_impl (follow-up handled in ENG-4877, but we should ensure the data exists).

Acceptance criteria
- For canary traffic, each request has runtime.kernel_set and runtime.attn_impl populated in telemetry.
- Kernel tags are stable for a given runtime build/config unless auto-selection changes due to a legitimate input bucket change.
- Metrics tag set passes cardinality audit (no explosion across models/regions).
- Oncall can answer within 5 minutes whether a regression coincides with a kernel set rollout or an impl switch.

Open questions
- Do we need runtime.prefill_attn_impl vs runtime.decode_attn_impl? (Some models diverge.)
  - Decision (2026-01-22): not in metrics initially; add trace-only split if we see ambiguous cases.
- Do we need a version for the selector heuristic separate from runtime.kernel_set?
  - Decision (2026-01-24): embed heuristic changes into runtime.kernel_set for now; revisit if we do selector-only rollouts.

Progress / updates
- 2026-01-18 (Hiro): Drafted tag set; requested telemetry cardinality review with Logan/Nadia.
- 2026-01-21 (Logan Wright): +1 on kernel_set concept; do not emit hashes/SHA. Keep impl enums tight. Any new impl value should be treated like a schema change.
- 2026-01-23 (Omar El-Sayed): Implemented plumbing from kernel selector to request context. Added guardrails to coerce unknown impls to "baseline" and emit a counter for investigation.
- 2026-01-28 (Hiro): Added trace-only kernel_select_reason behind sampling flag (default off for customer traffic; on for canary).
- 2026-02-03: Merged runtime changes in GitHub: sources/github/redwood/pr-19193-add-runtime-build-and-kernel-version-tags.json (includes kernel_set + impl tags; build tags handled in same PR).
- 2026-02-07: Verified canary metrics include kernel_set + attn_impl in us-east staging; no unexpected cardinality growth observed.
- 2026-02-12: Marking Done. Remaining work is dashboards consuming the dimensions + runbook callouts (tracked in ENG-4877 / ENG-4883).

Links
- Runtime PR: sources/github/redwood/pr-19193-add-runtime-build-and-kernel-version-tags.json
- Related: ENG-4873 (metric names/labels), ENG-4875 (queueing instrumentation), ENG-4877 (dashboards), ENG-4883 (runbook)

Notes for oncall
If perf-canary fires for a model:
1) Check if runtime.kernel_set changed around the start time.
2) If kernel_set unchanged, check runtime.attn_impl distribution for a shift (auto-selection change).
3) If impl shifted, correlate with recent runtime release notes and feature flags; consider rollback/disable of the kernel_set or forced_config override while kernels team investigates.
